subject: black ant
title: A Parasite Turns This Ant's Rear Into a Fake Red Berry

scenes.text: That red berry is actually part of an ant.
It's a black tree ant from the rainforest canopy of Panama.
Its abdomen is packed with hundreds of eggs from a parasitic worm. It turns red, and the ant holds it high.
The ant gets sluggish. The red part snaps off easily.
Scientists think that's the point: a bird mistakes it for fruit, eats it, and spreads the eggs in its droppings.
Ants feed those droppings to their young, and it starts again. It's the first parasite known to fake a fruit.

description:
In the rainforest canopy of Panama and Peru, a parasitic roundworm turns the black abdomen of the ant Cephalotes atratus bright red, like a ripe berry.
The infected ant carries hundreds of worm eggs, holds its abdomen raised, grows sluggish, and the abdomen breaks off easily. Researchers think fruit-eating birds swallow it and spread the eggs in their droppings, which the ants collect and feed to their larvae; nobody has yet watched a bird take one. Reported in 2008 in The American Naturalist as the first known case of a parasite making its host mimic fruit.
Cleverest parasite trick you have heard of? Comment below.
first_comment: About 5 percent of the workers in a colony carry the worm. Would you have spotted the fake berry?
